title: Hardware tail-behavior metrics and onboarding gates for device-specific profiles
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: When onboarding new model versions we publish a single performance profile per hardware SKU. Recent incidents show that tail behaviors (P95–P999) vary significantly across instances of the same SKU due to thermals, binning, and driver/platform differences. This causes customers to see regressions after pinning to a variant that looked fine in mean/median benchmarks but had unsafe tails.

Goal: Define a repeatable process and gating thresholds to capture device-specific tail-behavior metrics (latency and token-level throughput), integrate those metrics into the auto-pin recommender, and publish curated hardware profile artifacts that include tail-risk annotations for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants.

Scope: Collect and synthesize per-instance tail latency distributions and tail-throughput attenuation curves across the four target SKUs. Define onboarding gates (P90/P99/P999 thresholds relative to model baseline) and a confidence score for published profiles. Integrate annotations into the profile manifest exposed in the model catalog. Update pin recommender to penalize high tail-risk variants.

Non-goals: Changing kernel selection logic, implementing new thermal mitigation firmware, or altering pricing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated harvest job successfully collects P50/P90/P95/P99/P999 latency and tokens/sec distributions for each SKU across at least 30 instances per region.
2) Profile manifest includes fields: baseline_latency_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, p999_ms, tail_attenuation_pct, confidence_score, and recommended_pin_action.
3) Onboarding gate rules documented: fail-if p99 > baseline_p99 * 1.35 OR tail_attenuation_pct > 20%.
4) Pin recommender demonstrates lowered selection of high tail-risk variants in synthetic A/B test (delta in 99th-latency regressions < 5% after rollout).
5) Confluence doc and a follow-up runtime PR with end-to-end tests are merged.

2025-03-01 - Diego Morales: Ran synthetic A/B using 100K generated requests against candidate pin logic. Results: reduced P99 regressions by ~12% at cost of 3% median throughput loss on H100 variants.

notes: Tradeoffs discussed: stricter gates reduce customer surface area for regressions but increase model rollout friction. Chosen threshold is intentionally conservative for first rollout. We may relax after 2 successful release cycles.
